package_info.why_malicious: The package is a phishing kit that impersonates the official India Post website to deceive users into submitting sensitive personal and payment information. It uses cloned web pages and fraudulent forms to harvest PII and payment card data, which are then exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure for financial fraud and identity theft.

execution_context.trigger: When a user visits the phishing site via the provided link

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<form>
  <input name="name" type="text" required>
  <input name="address" type="text" required>
  <input name="email" type="email" required>
  <input name="phone" type="tel" required>
  <!-- Additional fields as seen in the phishing kit -->
</form>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user visits the phishing page via the phishing link, the code displays a web form that collects the user's name, address, email, and phone number, then transmits this PII to the attacker's backend server, resulting in unauthorized data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The form requests full PII from users on an unsolicited, non-official domain, which is a common tactic in phishing attacks to harvest sensitive information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate India Post websites do not request sensitive PII through unsolicited forms on unverified domains; such data collection would only occur after secure authentication and on official domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate government or e-commerce portals may collect PII, but only after user authentication and with clear, secure context on official domains.
key_indicators: Web form requesting full name, address, email, and phone number
Form hosted on a non-official, lookalike domain
No user authentication or verification before PII collection

execution_context.trigger: After the user submits PII and is redirected to the payment page

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<form>
  <input name="cardholder" type="text" required>
  <input name="cardnumber" type="text" required>
  <input name="expdate" type="text" required>
  <input name="cvv" type="password" required>
  <!-- Additional fields as seen in the phishing kit -->
</form>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the user submits their PII, the code presents a payment form that collects the cardholder's name, card number, expiration date, and CVV, then sends this payment card data to the attacker's backend, enabling theft of financial information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The form requests complete payment card details, including CVV, on a non-official domain for a minor fee, which is a hallmark of phishing scams targeting financial data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate India Post payment flows redirect users to trusted payment gateways and never request full card details, especially CVV, directly on non-official sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment forms exist but are only found on secure, verified domains and use established payment processors with visible security indicators.
key_indicators: Request for full cardholder name, card number, expiration date, and CVV
No integration with trusted payment gateway or processor
Payment form hosted on a suspicious, lookalike domain
No visible security features (e.g., HTTPS, trust seals)

execution_context.trigger: Upon form submission of PII or payment data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon submission of the PII or payment form, the JavaScript code sends the collected data via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled endpoint, resulting in immediate exfiltration of sensitive information to external infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive user data to an external, non-India Post endpoint, which is a defining characteristic of phishing kits designed for data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate sites process sensitive data internally or through trusted third-party processors, never by sending it to untrusted, unaffiliated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate sites may POST data to their own backend servers, but never to domains not affiliated with the service or lacking proper security controls.
key_indicators: JavaScript code making POST requests to external, attacker-controlled endpoints
No validation of recipient domain affiliation
No user notification or confirmation of data transfer
Absence of secure, official backend processing

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a phishing iMessage containing a short URL that claims a package is awaiting delivery from India Post.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim clicks the link and is directed to the phishing website.

attack_chain.action: The phishing site displays a cloned India Post interface and prompts the victim to enter personal information (name, address, email, phone).
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim submits PII and is redirected to the payment page.

attack_chain.action: The phishing site requests payment card details under the pretense of a small redelivery fee.
All collected PII and payment card data are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure via JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data for use in financial fraud or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Web forms on non-official domains requesting both PII and full payment card details
Cloned government or postal service branding presented on suspicious or recently registered domains
Immediate exfiltration of submitted form data to external, attacker-controlled endpoints via JavaScript
file_indicators: HTML forms containing input fields for name, address, email, phone, card number, and CVV on non-official domains
JavaScript code that performs fetch or XMLHttpRequest POSTs to domains not affiliated with India Post
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled endpoints immediately after form submission
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web traffic to known phishing domains and associated IPs, especially those mimicking India Post. Flag web forms on non-official domains that request both PII and payment card data. Detect JavaScript or HTML forms that POST sensitive data to external, non-India Post endpoints. Use threat intelligence feeds to block access to newly registered, lookalike domains and monitor for spikes in such registrations. Implement automated scanning for HTML/JS code patterns that collect and exfiltrate sensitive data to untrusted domains.
